source_review.notes: Checked current RFC Editor publications for Reno congestion control, CUBIC, new-algorithm evaluation, ECN, proportional-rate reduction, HyStart++, rate-limited traffic, QUIC control architecture and RACK-TLP, plus current Linux TCP sysctl documentation. All ten cited URLs returned HTTP 200 after normal redirects; normative algorithms, Linux controls, abstract hook models, operational guidance and assurance remain separately scoped.

evidence: Checked core state, event, private-state and output notation for congestion window, threshold, pace and diagnostics.
Reviewed send eligibility, bounded slow-start growth, delivery-rate samples, pacing clamps, lifecycle and callback generations.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation separates protocol truth, estimator inputs, algorithm-private state, transport safety envelopes and runtime lifecycle.

evidence: Executed MSS 1,200 with initial window 4,800 and three newly-acknowledged events of 1,200, 1,200 and 2,400 bytes.
Confirmed bounded windows 6,000, 7,200 and 8,400, then multiplicative loss response to threshold and window 4,200.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The deterministic computation validates one abstract growth and reduction sequence only; it implements no transport, loss detector, recovery, RTT, pacing, ECN, network or fairness.

evidence: Re-derived send eligibility as the minimum remaining congestion and receiver windows, ready data and pacing credit.
Checked ACK-byte growth cap, positive-interval rate estimate, widened pacing clamp and active-only lifecycle generation guard.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The relations are subsystem reasoning tools and do not claim a complete formalization of Reno, CUBIC, Linux hooks, BPF, QUIC or network dynamics.

evidence: Reviewed zero and maximum windows, MSS change, overflow, zero interval, ACK division, compression, reordering, retransmission ambiguity, application limitation and GSO.
Reviewed invalid plugin output, blocking callbacks, stale pointers, live switching, initialization failure, namespace changes, detach races and automatic fallback.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Signal, unit, arithmetic, sample, callback, policy, lifecycle, evaluation and rollback boundaries receive distinct treatment.

evidence: Traced validated transport facts through hook lifecycle, delivery, loss, ECN, pacing, startup, recovery, switching, detachment and fallback.

invariant_checking.notes: The chapter treats transport state, algorithm estimates, private memory, callback code, policy, scheduler and rollout as coupled but independently owned surfaces.

evidence: Reviewed core/plugin ownership, lifecycle callbacks, units, delivery, loss, ECN, rate samples, pacing, application limits, switching, runtime hooks and rollout.
Constructed counterexamples for cwnd-as-send-command, ACK-as-new-delivery, sample-as-capacity, verifier-as-fairness-proof and pointer-switch-as-state-migration.
proof_review.notes: The chapter supplies reusable hook obligations, not a formal proof of a controller, Linux, BPF runtime, network path, fairness or Internet safety.

evidence: Audited uses of acknowledged, delivered, lost, marked, sampled, limited, paced, initialized, selected, switched, detached and released.
Confirmed standards rules, Linux controls, abstract interfaces, recommendations, tests and assurance claims remain separately scoped.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: ACK arrival is not labeled new delivery, measured delivery is not labeled capacity, verifier acceptance is not labeled congestion safety and throughput is not labeled fairness.

evidence: artifacts/snippets/OS-077/report.json records source, expected and actual output, stderr, exit status, toolchain and environment for the bounded congestion-hook model.
Reviewed required controller, kernel, hook, socket, path, qdisc, device, cross-traffic, workload, fault and observer evidence.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The passing toy establishes one abstract window sequence only; it provides no evidence for protocol conformance, fairness, stability, kernel lifetime, deployment safety or performance.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed congestion-control extensibility as a narrow estimator interface inside a transport-core safety envelope with separately proved lifecycle and deployment obligations.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed current control mechanisms as implementable concerns, including delivery provenance, GSO-aware units, pacing, private-state ownership, transactional switching, runtime constraints and rollback. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from core signal ownership and lifecycle through delivery, loss, ECN, rate samples, pacing, modes, switching, policy, runtime hooks, evaluation and rollout, followed by twelve obligations, sixteen trade-offs, twenty-five misconceptions, ten examples and five complete exercises.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external operating-systems academic, IETF, Linux networking, congestion-control researcher, network-operator, security, performance, independent-verification or certification review is claimed.
